picks.excerpt: ETH Zurich researchers built PLATON, a particle detector that uses light-field camera optics and AI to reconstruct invisible particle tracks in 3D inside a single unsegmented block of scintillator. Simulations suggest it could match or surpass today's best detectors while being far simpler to scale.
picks.rationale: Novel AI-enabled detector architecture from a top lab (ETH); a genuinely new instrument approach, distinct from the already-published AMBer neutrino card, and credible via ScienceDaily — physics/instrumentation sub-domain.

picks.excerpt: A BERT-based machine-learning classifier screened 2.6 million cancer papers and flagged more than 250,000 with writing patterns resembling fraudulent 'paper mill' output, published in The BMJ. Suspect papers rose from about 1% in the early 2000s to more than 16% in 2022, exposing a large research-integrity problem.
picks.rationale: High-impact AI-for-research-integrity result published in The BMJ; broad relevance to how science is trusted, no prior coverage in the section, distinct sub-domain (meta-science / scientometrics). Second science pick given a distinct palette accent (#0070f3).

picks.excerpt: EMBL scientists used AI to design NovoTags, small de novo protein tags that bind fluorescent dyes so researchers can track specific proteins inside living cells. An inducible variant, NovoSplit, acts as a molecular switch and could distinguish up to 30 proteins at once by combining emission spectrum and fluorescence lifetime.
picks.rationale: Actionable, ready-to-use AI-designed lab tool for live-cell imaging from a leading institute (EMBL); a de novo protein-design result distinct from the already-published BetaDescribe (sequence-to-text) and SynTnpB (nuclease) cards. Third science pick gets a distinct palette accent (#7928ca) and shifts outlet to Phys.org.

picks.excerpt: Researchers developed an AI-enhanced rare-event sampling framework (AI+RES) that predicts the frequency of extreme heatwaves using up to 1000 times less compute than conventional climate modeling. The AI directs full physics-based models to simulate only the high-probability scenarios, bridging deep-learning efficiency with physical reliability.
picks.rationale: Novel hybrid AI + physics method with a concrete 1000x compute win for extreme-weather prediction; credible (Physics World), climate/earth-science sub-domain, and adds a third distinct outlet to the mix. Distinct palette accent (#f5a623).

picks.excerpt: A Rutgers-led team built an AI system that continuously monitors mouse locomotor activity and applies machine learning to flag health problems, detecting issues 3-5 days before obvious clinical signs appeared. The tool, reported in Lab Animal, aims to improve welfare and reliability in laboratory animal research.
picks.rationale: Practical AI monitoring tool with an early-detection edge (3-5 days) that changes how labs run animal studies; life-science / research-practice sub-domain, no prior coverage. Fifth pick; distinct palette accent (#eb367f). Second Phys.org card, holding the outlet cap at 2.
